379YE Spring Equinox Announcements by th.d: The Crystal Architect commissioned two mana sinecures, each costing 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour, with no upkeep. Tiberius EchoStorm provided the full materials and labour for both after the Spring Equinox. When complete, the Caves of the Claw create the title of Custodian of the Claw, and the Tower of the Fall creates the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall. Both are national positions appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators, serving for life or until revoked. The Caves were to be built in Morrow. Construction of the Tower had not begun, because the Crystal Architect had been unable to provide the relevant information.

n.Urizen: Urizen stands to gain two new national titles, the Custodian of the Claw and the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall, both appointed by unanimous vote of its senators, and Tiberius EchoStorm funded both projects in full.

t.Morrow: The Caves of the Claw, a mana sinecure overseen by the Custodian of the Claw, were commissioned in Morrow and fully funded; the region was not specified.
t.Zenith: The Tower of the Fall, a mana sinecure for the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall, was commissioned for Zenith, but construction had not begun because the Crystal Architect could not supply the needed information.

379YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: New senators were returned for Segura (Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra), Holberg (Rossalyn Jordan), Karsk (Radomir) and Skarsind (Thanmir Hrafn), alongside several Senate appointments including the Advisor on Orc Affairs and the Ambassador to Jarm. Generals were chosen for the Fire of the South, the Valiant Pegasus and the Summer Storm. The Synod elected Cardinals of Ambition, Prosperity and Vigilance, four Gatekeepers, the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability, the Imperial Inquisitor and the Chaplain Consular. Cyrus, son of Felix, became Imperial Magus. Bourse seats and national titles changed hands, including the Master of the Imperial Mint and the Steel Fist.

n.Dawn: Lady Josephine Novarion of Dawn was chosen as Gatekeeper of Pride in the Synod.
n.Highguard: Highborn took several religious and magical posts: Silas of the Suns of Couros became Cardinal of Vigilance, Seraiah Armand became Gatekeeper of Ambition, Sargon of Felix's Watch became Auditor of Senatorial Accountability and Cyrus, son of Felix, became Imperial Magus.
n.Imperial Orcs: The national title of the Steel Fist passed to Irontide Kul.
n.Navarr: Hywel Summercrow of Navarr was appointed Chaplain Consular.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gained a new senator for Segura, and the Broken Shore Bounty went to Karlos i Shartha i Riqueza.
n.The League: League citizens took prominent offices: Olek La Maschera Sorridente de Temeschwar became Cardinal of Ambition, Severin Teyhard von Holberg became Imperial Inquisitor, Fererro became Master of the Imperial Mint and Rodrigo Barossa took the Regario Dossier.
n.Varushka: Varushkans took two Synod gatekeeper posts, with Wilhemina Maryenkovich Poltova for Prosperity and Nikolovich Drakov for Vigilance, and Radomir became senator for Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Edythe Dunne of Wintermark became Cardinal of Prosperity, Ogmundr Kaldrheim took the Stonefield Ice Caves and Thanmir Hrafn became senator for Skarsind.

t.Holberg: Rossalyn Jordan was returned as senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: Radomir was returned as senator for Karsk.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra was returned as senator for Segura.
t.Skarsind: Thanmir Hrafn was returned as senator for Skarsind.

379YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Two opportunities were noted: auras of Prosperity in Hahnmark's mines, which drew workers away from other businesses, and a fungus in Miaren that harmed herb gardens but was valued by farmers as a livestock medicine. In Wintermark, the Bane of Tradition set Suaq, Kallavesi and Steinr against one another and strained the Fist of the Mountains and Green Shield. Thule sorcery was the likely culprit. Kallavesa's crystal mana was halved by something separate, and Sermersuaq suffered storms and a Winter magnitude 15 effect that halved its mana. A Winter curse of magnitude 50 blighted Liathaven, Hercynia, Miaren and Therunin, damaging every kind of production before lifting. In Karsk, husk wolves gathered around a ruined fort.

n.Navarr: A Winter curse of magnitude 50 struck only the Navarr, damaging herbs, mines, forests, businesses, congregations, soldiers' equipment and mana sites in four of their territories. Only the draughir were left strangely untroubled.
n.Thule: The Thule were named as the most likely source of the Bane of Tradition, since dividing Wintermark served their invasion. They were also noted as fighting the Varushkans in Karsk.
n.Varushka: Varushka's war with the Thule in Karsk was complicated by reports of husk wolves gathering in western Lestazny, though so far they had not attacked.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was beset by the Bane of Tradition, which turned its three traditions against one another and threatened the cohesion of its armies. Mana failures in Kallavesa and Sermersuaq added to the strain alongside the Thule invasion.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: noted as the one Navarr territory that appeared to have been spared the cursed winter.
t.Hahnmark: Miraculous auras of Prosperity arose in Hahnmark's mines, boosting mining output but leaving local businesses short of labour. This was presented as an opportunity for a response.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia was battered by the cursed Navarr winter, suffering blight, accidents, ruined stores, sickness and reduced production across its resources.
t.Kallavesa: Roughly half of Kallavesa's crystal mana formed dull and useless, and portents suggested a cause separate from the rift between the traditions.
t.Karsk: Husk wolves made from recent and long-buried corpses gathered around a ruined fort on an old battlefield in western Lestazny. They had not yet attacked any settlements.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven suffered the cursed Navarr winter, with terrible weather, misfortune and sabotaged mana sites cutting its production.
t.Miaren: After an autumn of prosperity, Miaren was hit by the cursed winter. A rare fungus was also harming its herb gardens while being prized by farmers as a livestock remedy, which was presented as an opportunity.
t.Sermersuaq: Unseasonable storms and a Winter magnitude 15 effect halved Sermersuaq's mana production. Its magicians suffered depression, lethargy or bouts of aggression.
t.Therunin: Therunin was among the four Navarr territories struck by the cursed winter, losing production to bad weather, blight and supernatural misfortune.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Battle continued in the Silver Peaks, and magicians accompanying the armies there were affected by the same restless, wintry malaise as the rest of Sermersuaq.

379YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: In Holberg, around 36,000 Imperial troops broke the siege of Rebeshof and razed the fortress. They then took Ennerlund and the Morass, despite Druj curses of pestilence and possessed trees. Nearly four thousand Imperial soldiers fell against some eight thousand Druj. A Senate motion of Assignment is now needed. In Karsk the Thule withdrew and both magical citadels were Imperial. In Reikos, Riverwatch, Haros Water and the Vigilant Swan were freed as the Druj fell back to High Chalcis under a pall of dread. In Sermersuaq, Thule sorcery and eternal knights gained ground slowly at the cost of about 1,500 Imperial dead. Fifty companies fought abroad in Faraden and Ipotavo, and storms battered Grendel shipping off Spiral.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun hunted Druj agents across Holberg and lost about four hundred yeomen and nobles. Meanwhile the Hounds of Glory in Sermersuaq were cheered by rumours that Dawn would soon campaign into the Barrens after the destruction of the Spires of Dusk.
n.Druj: The Druj suffered a crushing defeat in Holberg: about eight thousand dead, the scorpion banner shattered and Rebeshof destroyed. In Reikos they fell back to their citadel at High Chalcis, though they still besiege Ipotavo with around ten thousand orcs.
n.Grendel: Massive storms off Spiral impeded Grendel shipping and prevented any naval reinforcement. Their scouts were spotted in Screed, and an interlude shows Kallavesi raiders attacking a Grendel ship despite the Senate's suggestion not to.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus led the liberation of Riverwatch, Haros Water and the Vigilant Swan, laying the remains of murdered Highborn to rest as they went. Two Highborn captains also joined the defence of Ipotavo.
n.Jotun: Thirty Imperial companies joined General Jekal Swordborn of House Ogudai to drive the Jotun from the hills of Tebukan in Faraden. The outcome remains to be seen.
n.Navarr: The Navarr suffered no significant casualties in Karsk, where the Black Thorns' unliving husks rotted away by the Equinox. In Reikos the Quiet Step suffered from festering wounds, and five Navarr captains fought at Ipotavo.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South withdrew from Sermersuaq. The Red Wind Corsairs raided Thule parties there, shielded by unliving allies and growing rich on plunder, to the scorn of the Winterfolk who called them maggots.
n.The League: The Wolves of War spearheaded the reconquest of Holberg, returning it to the Empire for the first time in thirty years amid cautious League rejoicing. Several hundred League miners died in the collapse of the Great Pits, and the Towerjacks met privately about taking the field again.
n.Thule: In Karsk the Thule avoided battle and fell back east and north, showing little of their magic. In Sermersuaq, eternal knights of Tykonus and Feresh, monstrous beasts and potent sorcery let them slowly claim another portion of the Silver Peaks.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard advised on Holberg's curses, and Urizen sentinels held the breach at Rebeshof. Ten Urizen captains joined the defence of Ipotavo, and in Spiral the Black Plateau stayed quiescent while Grendel scouts appeared in Screed.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle held Karsk without significant losses and was strengthened by weapons and recruits from the Moresvah miners. However, Varushka's backwoods allies in Branoc suffered defeat after defeat against the Thule, and two Varushkan captains fought at Ipotavo.
n.Wintermark: The Green Shield and Fist of the Mountains fought side by side in Sermersuaq, eight thousand Winterfolk defending their home. Tensions between the Steinr, Kallavesi and Suaq made it ever harder to keep the armies together.

t.Casinea: An interlude showed Dawnish knights of the Eastern Sky, billeted in Casinea after their victory in Segura, comically berating a Highborn cook over steamed puddings and water.
t.Holberg: The Empire took Holfried, Holmauer, Rebeshof, Ennerlund and the Morass, though Druj curses of pestilence and possessed trees persist. A Senate motion of Assignment, and possibly one of Allocation for the Great Pits, must now follow.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi sea-raider in an interlude complains that the nights in Kallavesa are cold and they have no ilium.
t.Karsk: Karsk remained Imperial, with both magical citadels now held by the Empire and the hills running green under the spring enchantment. No significant territory changed hands as the Thule withdrew.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: great blind apes from caverns beneath the mountains of Otkodov fought alongside the Thule in Sermersuaq.
t.Reikos: Imperial forces pushed west as the Druj retreated to High Chalcis, freeing Riverwatch, Haros Water and the ruined Vigilant Swan quarry. A dread miasma and false stars continued to slow the liberation.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights in an interlude are described as having come victorious from Segura.
t.Sermersuaq: The deadlock continued: about 20,000 Imperial defenders held against an overwhelming Thule assault, but were slowly pushed back in the Silver Peaks with some fifteen hundred dead.
t.Spiral: Storms off Spiral's coast blocked Grendel naval reinforcement, and the Black Plateau remained quiescent with some of its afflicted slowly recovering. Grendel scouts in Screed prompted the Urizen to begin preparations.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Empire took Ennerlund after a vicious battle and found the Great Pits collapsed and trapped, with several hundred League miners buried alive. Civil servants are now reporting on whether the mines can be reopened.
r.Holberg/Holfried: Marchers passing through visited the war memorial at Holfried, and the surviving Towerjacks commanders held a closed meeting in its garrison about their future.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer's remaining parks were closed and guarded against the possessed trees. A column of Autumn-realm mercenaries arrived through a regio here.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde's trees were infused with malignant spirits, and the fleeing Druj banners retreated into its deep northern forests, which remain beyond Imperial control.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: After a three-week siege the Imperial armies breached Rebeshof and killed nearly two thousand Druj. The fortress was reduced to worse than rubble, and the region was claimed for the Empire.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's trees were cursed with malignant spirits, and the Druj fled into its deep forests after a costly pitched battle on the forest edge. The region remains beyond the Imperial line.
r.Karsk/Branoc: The backwoods folk of Branoc fought on against the Thule without Imperial army support and suffered heavy losses and repeated defeats.
r.Karsk/Kopevnost: The Black Thorns sheltered in the safe havens of Kopevnost, defending Imperial territory rather than seeking battle.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: An Imperial citadel of ice and ivory stood in southern Moresvah. The region's miners used the lull to deliver ten wagons of arms and new recruits to the Northern Eagle.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: The magical fortress of ice and granite in northern Nitrost belonged to the Empire, providing a safe haven for Imperial armies.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Imperial forces pushed into Haros Water and fought for three nights in the ruins of Haros town before the retreating Druj set it ablaze.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The Empire seized the ruins of Tabernacle and claimed Riverwatch, purging the Druj ambushers left behind.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Mentioned in passing: the roar of the fiery draconic sigil above the northern peaks was heard as far as East Floes.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks bore the brunt of the Thule assault, and the barbarians claimed another portion of the region. The healing spring waters there lay frozen in ice, and a fiery draconic omen blazed over the northernmost peak.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Mentioned in passing: the roar of the fiery sigil over the northern peaks was heard in Suaq Fount.
r.Spiral/Screed: The night magician Causus reported Grendel scouts in Screed, suggesting the barbarians know the Black Plateau has been neutralised.

A Blight in Miaren.d: Navarr walking the trods of Miaren reported sudden blights of Armillaria, a white, furry fungus suspected of being altered by the realm of Spring. It aggressively attacks marrowort, harming herb gardens, but acts as a natural medicinal for livestock, improving farm productivity. The fungus is fragile, lasting only until the Summer Solstice and unlikely to spread beyond adjacent territories, and worldblood (ambergelt) is toxic to it. The civil service set out several options: Senate motions to harvest the fungus for livestock or deliberately spread it to neighbouring territories, a Conclave gambit of ambergelt to kill it, approaching the Eternal Llofir, or using the ritual Ruthless Vigilance, Healthy Crop. Mari, Archmage of Day, rallied the Conclave to gather ambergelt and destroy the infestation.

n.Navarr: Navarr trod-walkers first reported the blight in their territory of Miaren, threatening Navarr herb gardens' marrowort while offering a temporary boon to their farms before the Conclave's ambergelt destroyed the fungus.

t.Miaren: Armillaria fungus spread through Miaren's herb gardens, threatening marrowort yields while potentially benefiting local livestock, until the Conclave gathered ambergelt to eliminate the blight and both its harms and benefits.

A Miracle in Hahnmark.d: Miners in Hahnmark's weltsilver mines reported warm, enjoyable sensations when working the ore, greatly increasing productivity. Religious zeal and congregation attendance rose, but other businesses complained of losing workers to the mines. Some speculated the auras stemmed from a forgotten Wintermark Paragon of Prosperity, sparking debate over whether they were Kallavesi, Steinr or Suaq. The civil service offered options including a recruitment subsidy for businesses, spreading the effect to all mines, missionary work to an adjacent territory, or a controversial exorcism. A General Assembly judgement of Rewarding sent Jorma Steelhail to spread word to Skarsind, and a Prosperity Assembly judgement sent Soratio Seseer Del Toro so that all mines in the affected territories would benefit.

n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: a historical Cardinal of the Way, an Urizen Illuminate suspected of Lucidianism, is cited as having once called for the exorcism of a spontaneous aura of Ambition.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's mining territories gained a miraculous boost to mine output and congregational influence, and the auras prompted speculation about a forgotten Wintermark Paragon of Prosperity, with debate over whether they were Kallavesi, Steinr or Suaq.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's weltsilver mines became the source of spontaneous Prosperity auras, raising mine productivity and congregation attendance, though local businesses complained of losing labour to the mines; a Prosperity Assembly judgement sought to extend the benefit to all mines there.
t.Skarsind: Through a General Assembly judgement of Rewarding, Jorma Steelhail was charged with spreading word of the miracle to neighbouring Skarsind so that it too would share in the effect.

Allocate the Vigilant Swan.d: The Vigilant Swan in Reikos had recently been liberated by Imperial troops. A motion proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Casinea sought to allocate the bourse seat. Highguard and the Imperial Orcs were both proposed, and the Senate passed it as a national position assigned to the Imperial Orcs. The General Assembly of the Imperial Synod then vetoed the motion, so it could not be raised again that summit. The Swan remained unassigned, with production from Spring 379YE stockpiled for the first Imperial citizen elected to operate it. Had the motion stood, the seat's national status would have followed whichever nation Reikos was eventually assigned to.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, though the Vigilant Swan is described as recently liberated by Imperial troops in Reikos, a territory they held.
n.Highguard: Highguard was proposed as a nation to receive the Vigilant Swan, and the motion was put forward by the senators for Necropolis and Casinea, but the seat was assigned to the Imperial Orcs before the Synod's veto overturned it.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Senate assigned the Vigilant Swan to the Imperial Orcs as a national position, but the Synod's veto denied them the seat, leaving it unassigned.

t.Reikos: The Vigilant Swan bourse seat in Reikos, recently liberated by Imperial troops, was left unassigned after the veto, with its output stockpiled for its first elected holder.

Amend powers of Dredgemaster of Feverwat.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Hercynia, the motion amended the powers of the Dredgemaster of Feverwater, the sinecure dedicated to dredging lake Feverwater in Therunin. The Senate set no upper limit on improving the sinecure. The Dredgemaster may announce one historical research request each season to the Civil Service, which presents it to the Senate without a vote, though the Synod may veto it. The Empire's overall seasonal limit on historical research still applies. Because similar titles are appointed annually, the Constitutional Court recommended the title's tenure become annual. This power was later removed by the Senate at the Winter Solstice 381YE.

n.Navarr: The improved sinecure is based in Navarri-held Therunin, and its holder gained the power to direct a share of the Empire's historical research each season, until the Senate removed that power in Winter 381YE.

t.Therunin: The sinecure dredging lake Feverwater in Therunin was to be improved, and the Dredgemaster overseeing it gained the power to commission one piece of historical research each season.

Archive:379YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: The list named the senators for each Imperial territory and the holders of other Senate posts, such as Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg as Conscience of the Senate. It also named the generals and officers of the Military Council, the cardinals, gatekeepers and other Synod post-holders, and the Archmagi and Grandmasters of the Conclave. The Imperial and national Bourse seats were listed with their holders and, where recorded, the price paid in thrones. Two seats were not allocated. The Great Forest at Reikos remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until Reikos was Imperial again. The Great Pits of Ennerlund needed repair before allocation, now that Holberg was once more an Imperial territory.

n.Dawn: Dawn held senators for Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater and three generals, including Tancred de Rondell of the Hounds of Glory. Its people also included Cardinal Agnetha De Rondell of Wisdom and Gatekeeper Lady Josephine Novarion of Pride.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj still held the Great Forest at Reikos, and they had previously held the Great Pits of Ennerlund.
n.Highguard: Highguard held senators for Bastion, Casinea and Necropolis and three generals. Its people also filled several Synod roles, including Cardinals Asher, Jared and Silas and the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs fielded General Morgur Bloodcrow of the Winter Sun and General Irontide Skar of the Summer Storm. Irontide Kul held the national Bourse seat of the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Navarr held senators for Hercynia, Miaren and Therunin and generals Carr Foxden and Merryn Farkas. Its people also included Hywel Summercrow as Chaplain Consular and Idris Eternal, holder of the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held senators for Feroz, Kahraman, Madruga and Segura and two generals. Sendero i Hazana i Guerra served as Admiral, and Karlos i Shartha i Riqueza held the Broken Shore Bounty.
n.The League: The League held senators for Holberg, Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar and General Gabriel Barossa of the Wolves of War. Leaguers also held several Bourse seats and the posts of Conscience of the Senate and Imperial Inquisitor.
n.The Marches: The Marches held senators for Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and three generals, of the Drakes, the Strong Reeds and the Bounders.
n.Urizen: Urizen held senators for Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith and General Tanwyn Ankarien of the Citadel Guard. Its people also included Solas as High Exorcist and Livia Cascade as Gatekeeper of Wisdom.
n.Varushka: Varushka held senators for Karsk, Karov, Miekarova and Volodmartz and two generals. Varushkans held many Synod roles, including Cardinal Elka Nadyanova Gremani of Pride, as well as the national Bourse seats of the Eternal Shafts of Time and the Granites of Veltsgorsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held senators for Hahnmark, Kallavesa, Sermersuaq and Skarsind and generals of the Green Shield Army and the Fist of the Mountain. Its people also included Cardinal Edythe Dunne of Prosperity and Bishop Beodun Snowlock of the Way.

t.Astolat: Hector de Rondell sat as Senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Jada of Ravensfell sat as Senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick sat as Senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold sat as Senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Kattalin i Hazama i Guerra sat as Senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun sat as Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Rhain sat as Senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Rossalyn Jordan sat as Senator for Holberg, which was once again an Imperial territory.
t.Kahraman: Zamira i Covas i Erigo sat as Senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Uskolli sat as Senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Constantin sat as Senator for Karov.
t.Karsk: Radomir sat as Senator for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Anwar i Del-Toro i Riquezza sat as Senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Syn Nighthaven sat as Senator for Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Dušan Otecovna Zlata sat as Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville sat as Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne sat as Senator for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Adamah of the Silent Tide sat as Senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Marissa Shatterspire sat as Senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Reikos had no senator listed, and its Great Forest remained in Druj hands. The seat would not be auctioned until Reikos was once again an Imperial territory.
t.Sarvos: Mirislav sat as Senator for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra sat as Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Escalados deCarsenere sat as Senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte sat as Senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Thanmir Hrafn sat as Senator for Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato sat as Senator for Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Gant Archama sat as Senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Caerwyn Summer Crow sat as Senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward sat as Senator for Upwold, the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Irina Kardaova Arkady sat as Senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel sat as Senator for Weirwater, and the Bourse seat of the Weirwater Vales was held by Landon of Longridge for 280 thrones.
t.Zenith: Cato sat as Senator for Zenith.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund, formerly held by the Druj, needed repairing before the seat could be allocated, now that Holberg was Imperial again.

Assignment of Holberg.d: The motion that Holberg be allocated to the League was proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by the senator for Astolat. An alternative was put forward that Holberg instead be assigned to the Imperial Orcs. The Senate passed the motion in favour of the League by 19 votes to 11. As a result, Holberg was assigned to the League and gained the right to elect a Senator to represent it.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were the subject of a rival proposal to receive Holberg, but the Senate voted against them, so the territory did not pass into orc hands.
n.The League: The League was awarded Holberg by 19 votes to 11, adding a territory to its lands and gaining the right to elect a Senator for it.

t.Holberg: Holberg was formally assigned to the League rather than the Imperial Orcs and became entitled to elect its own Senator.

Construct Hordalant spy network.d: The motion called for a spy network in Hordalant, costing 10 weirwood, taking three months to construct and requiring 2 Thrones a season in upkeep from the Senate budget. Caerwyn supplied the 10 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice 379YE, and the network was finished shortly before the Autumn Equinox. Imperial citizens could assign military units to it: five units would reveal a map of settlements, ten the armies, naval routes and trading partners, and fifteen the location and size of fortifications. Contributors received the information and a share of the Imperial guerdon. Historical research on Emperor Guntherm's reign recorded a Marcher attempt to capture Hordalant.

n.Jotun: The spy network was built in Jotun-controlled Hordalant, so Imperial units supporting it could uncover the territory's settlements, Jotun armies, naval routes, trading partners and fortifications.
n.The Marches: The motion recalled historical research showing that Marcher forces under Emperor Guntherm once tried to capture Hordalant from the border of Bregasland but stalled after taking Blutgahn and Ashahohn.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is described as lying on the border of Bregasland in the historical account cited by the motion.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant became the site of an Imperial spy network, completed before the Autumn Equinox 379YE, through which units could gather intelligence on its settlements, armies, trade and fortifications.

r.Hordalant/Blutgahn: Mentioned in passing: the historical account notes that Marchers once overran the marshes of Blutgahn during Emperor Guntherm's reign.

Construct House of Barbs.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Miaren, the motion passed at 1 ring. Construction required 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, with no upkeep. Bloody Trees Rhain Winters Vigil supplied the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and the House of Barbs was completed, leaving the Voice of Barbs to be appointed. The title is normally held for life and grants Synod membership, including the relevant assemblies. In Summer 382YE, after an earlier false start, the Senate commissioned an extension that increased the liao and votes the sinecure provides. The Constitution notes also warned senators against motions of similar verbosity.

n.Navarr: The Navarr national assembly gains the right to elect the Voice of Barbs, a title carrying 12 Synod votes, and the building was funded by the Navarr Bloody Trees Rhain Winters Vigil.

t.Hercynia: The House of Barbs was built in Hercynia, using white granite and crowns supplied after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and was later extended in 382YE.

Construct Iron Confederacy embassy.d: The motion granted permission to build an Iron Confederacy embassy in Sarvos. Its construction was passed at 187 thrones. The standard cost was 25 wains of weirwood and 25 wains of white granite, plus 12 thrones of labour, with one season's construction time and an upkeep of 5 thrones. Miroslav provided the weirwood, granite and labour money after the Spring Equinox 379YE. Once complete, the embassy would automatically create the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.

n.The League: The League's senator for Sarvos proposed the embassy, placing the Empire's diplomatic link to the Iron Confederacy within a League territory.

t.Sarvos: The Iron Confederacy embassy was to be built in Sarvos, with materials and labour supplied by Miroslav after the Spring Equinox.

Construct Printers' Guild Museum of Wond.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Semmerholm in Spring 379YE, the motion created a museum sinecure appointed by the Cardinal of Prosperity, providing 6 liao and 12 Synod votes to its Curator. It required 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns of labour, both supplied by Silvio de Tassato. As first written, the motion was unconstitutional because it could let a citizen vote in a virtue assembly they did not belong to. The Senate agreed amendments at the Autumn Equinox 379YE summit making it a lifetime appointment by the current Cardinal of Prosperity, with votes in the assemblies matching the holder's nationality and virtue. On completion it created the title Curator of the Printers' Guild Museum.

n.The League: The League gained a new cultural institution and Synod title in one of its cities, built with materials and funds supplied by Silvio de Tassato and championed by Tassato's senator.

t.Tassato: The Printers' Guild Museum of Wonders was built in the city of Tassato, giving the printers' guild collection of relics and artefacts a permanent public home there.

Construct Sumaah embassy II.d: The motion followed the defeat of a similar vote in Winter 378YE and passed at 0 Thrones. The embassy required 25 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 12 Thrones of labour and one season to build, with upkeep of 5 Thrones. Lucifer Son of Cyrus supplied 20 wains each of weirwood and white granite after the Summer Solstice 379YE. Cyrus, son of Felix supplied the remaining 5 wains of each and 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Once complete, the embassy would automatically create the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

n.Highguard: The Empire's embassy to the Sumaah Republic was to be raised on Highguard soil in Necropolis, with that territory's senator seconding the motion.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis was chosen as the site of the Sumaah Republic embassy, and its senator seconded the motion permitting its construction.

Construct cargo dock at Caricomare.d: Proposed by Holberg and seconded by Mitwold, the motion sought a dock at Caricomare that would provide 20 white granite per season through trade with the Asaveans. A Synod veto was threatened but was not possible, because the Synod had already used that power earlier in the summit. The project cost 30 wains of weirwood and 10 wains of white granite. Ros Jordan supplied the granite after the Summer Solstice 379YE. The dock's benefit depended on the co-operation of Asavean merchants, and Alonso Tarquinius brought undisclosed Asavean expectations to Anvil. Completion would have created a new Imperial title, though not an extra Bourse seat. Grendel orc pillagers destroyed the partially built docks during their invasion of Sarvos.

n.Grendel: Grendel pillagers invading Sarvos destroyed the partially constructed Caricomare docks, wiping out all progress on the project.
n.The League: The League's Caricomare would have gained a cargo dock and an associated Bourse title through Asavean trade, but its investment was lost when Grendel orcs razed the unfinished docks.

t.Sarvos: The cargo dock was being built on the Caricomare docks in Sarvos until the Grendel invasion of the territory destroyed the partial construction.

Declare peace with Barrens orcs.d: The motion, proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, granted the orcs of the Barrens all the legal protections and responsibilities of foreigners under Imperial law. The stated aim was to open negotiations with the three tribes that had once served the Druj and now occupied the Barrens. Because they were recognised as foreigners, any invasion of their lands by Imperial troops would become a criminal offence while that status stood. By the end of Spring 379YE the orcs of the Barrens had made no official response to the declaration.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the three Barrens tribes are described as having previously been subservient to the Druj, and the motion treats them as separate from their former masters.

t.The Barrens: The orcs occupying the Barrens became foreigners under Imperial law, making any invasion of their lands by Imperial troops a criminal offence. By the end of the season they had made no official response.

Disburse funds to the Jarmish Cartel.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Kahraman, the motion asked the Senate to approve the Jarmish Cartel. The cartel sought to trade exclusively with the new port of Eastern Jarm. In return it would virtuously release its slaves held in contract within one year. The motion requested 50 thrones to cover the agreement with Eastern Jarm, but it passed at 35 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Segura. The port in question was Rigia, which had recently opened to the Empire after the completion of the Jarmish Embassy in Cargo.

n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Urizen directly; its link appears to come through the senators who proposed and seconded the motion.

t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the page does not refer to Redoubt directly; its connection is presumably through the senators involved in the motion.

Fortify Miekarova II.d: The motion called for a new fortification, Grimhold, to be built in the Vale of Strascovia, home of the Vor'Azi people, using the crumbling ruins of their ancestral castle as its foundation. The standard cost was 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones, with a year to construct and upkeep of 10 thrones per season. Dušan Otecovna Zlata supplied 40 wains of white granite and 20 thrones after the Spring Equinox 379YE, and a further 40 wains after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, meeting the full material cost. Once complete, it will give Miekarova a rank one fortification. A previous motion to fortify the territory had been defeated in Winter 378YE.

n.Varushka: Varushkans renewed their effort to fortify one of their own territories after an earlier defeat, with Dušan Otecovna Zlata personally providing all the granite and thrones the work required.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova is to gain its first fortification, Grimhold, a rank one fortress, once the year-long construction is complete, at an ongoing upkeep of 10 thrones per season.

r.Miekarova/Perumaki: Grimhold is being raised in Perumaki's Vale of Strascovia, built on the crumbling ruins of the Vor'Azi people's ancestral castle.

Raise Dawnish army II.d: The motion passed at a cost of 500 Thrones, disbursed to Senator Weirwater, and required 250 wains of mithril and a year of construction, with upkeep of 50 Thrones per season once complete. Valentin Ivarovich Severyan supplied the mithril over the following year: 60 wains after the Spring Equinox, 60 after the Summer Solstice, 65 after the Autumn Equinox, and 76 wains plus 19 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. With the materials delivered, the recorded outcome was that a new Dawnish army would muster in Semmerholm.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained Senate approval for a new army, to be added to its military strength once construction finished, at an ongoing upkeep of 50 Thrones per season.

t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was chosen as the mustering ground for the new Dawnish army raised under this motion.

Raise Wintermark army.d: In Spring 379YE the Senate was asked to permit the Winterfolk to begin raising a new army, reformed as the Bloodcloaks, a Grimnir-laden army focused on physick. The motion would have carried all the standard costs of raising a new army. The original Bloodcloaks were a Wintermark army famed for their crimson cloaks and made up of many grimnir and mystics. They were lost to the Thule during the reign of Empress Brannan, when all but a few were slaughtered in a disastrous retreat from Otkodov. The motion was withdrawn after the Senate passed a motion to let the Dawnish raise an army instead, so no new Wintermark army was raised.

n.Thule: The Thule are named as the destroyers of the original Bloodcloaks, who were wiped out during a retreat from Otkodov in Empress Brannan's reign.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators for Hahnmark and Bregasland sought to restore the lost Bloodcloaks as a grimnir-heavy army. The motion was withdrawn once a Dawnish army motion passed, leaving Wintermark without its new force.

t.Otkodov: Otkodov was the scene of the disastrous retreat in which nearly all of the original Bloodcloaks were slaughtered by the Thule.

Relinquish Skarsind.d: The Winterfolk senators presented the relinquishment as an act of loyalty to the Empire and to the Imperial Orcs. The Constitutional Court judged it to represent the true will of Wintermark, given its senators' unanimous support and the Wintermark Assembly's right of veto. It could be abrogated by the Senate before ratification, or vetoed by the Assembly of the Nine, the General Assembly or the Wintermark National Assembly before the first Senate session of the Summer Solstice. The Brilliant Shore Bourse seat would stay with Wintermark until reassignment. At the Autumn Equinox 379YE the Imperial Favour of Empress Britta allowed ratification without a Throne, and the Senate assigned Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs. The motion led directly to the Senate's power of relinquishment.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators voluntarily gave up their nation's claim to Skarsind out of loyalty to the Empire and the Imperial Orcs, keeping the Brilliant Shore Bourse seat only until the territory was reassigned, and the Wintermark National Assembly was given its own power to veto the motion.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind was to cease being part of Wintermark, and after the motion was ratified at the Autumn Equinox 379YE through Empress Britta's Imperial Favour, the Senate assigned it to the Imperial Orcs as their first home.

Repair Great Pits of Ennerlund.d: After Imperial forces liberated the Great Pits of Ennerlund, the Senate voted at Spring 379YE to repair the mines. The Druj had collapsed them in Winter 378YE and destroyed the pumping mechanisms, causing great loss of life and leaving the workings inoperable. The repair required 250 thrones of materials and nine months. Bridget Eastville of the Marches provided the 250 thrones after the Spring Equinox. Mithril was first expected after the Spring Equinox 380YE, but an extensive haunting of the mines delayed production by a season, with the first mithril due at the Autumn Equinox 380YE. The Great Pits were fully repaired, returning to their pre-destruction output of 27 wains of mithril a season.

n.Druj: The Druj sabotage of Winter 378YE, which collapsed the pits and wrecked the pumps at great cost in lives, was undone by the Imperial repair.
n.The League: The League's Holberg regained a major mithril mine, restored to its full output of 27 wains a season after the Druj destruction.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Bridget Eastville of the Marches provided the 250 thrones that paid for the repairs.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Great Pits, liberated from the Druj, were rebuilt over nine months. A haunting delayed the first mithril until the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The collapsed mineworkings at Ennerlund were repaired despite an extensive haunting, and the pits returned to producing 27 wains of mithril a season.
